title: PowerRChol: Efficient Power Grid Analysis Based on Fast Randomized Cholesky Factorization
problem: Power grid analysis requires solving large linear equations with millions of unknowns, which is computationally challenging. Existing preconditioning approaches suffer from either high construction costs or slow convergence rates, resulting in unsatisfactory total solution time.
motivation: Efficient power grid analysis is critical for modern VLSI design.
method: PowerRChol uses a randomized Cholesky factorization (a way to break down matrices that uses randomness to speed things up) with linear-time complexity to create a preconditioner—a transformed version of the problem designed to be faster to solve. It reorders the matrix elements to improve how the computer accesses memory and speeds up how quickly the solution converges. The preconditioned problem is then solved using Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient solvers (iterative solvers that repeatedly improve the answer), efficiently handling the sparse linear systems with millions of equations that power grids generate.
key_novelty: Randomized Cholesky factorization with linear-time complexity that delivers both fast preconditioner construction and fast solver convergence, overcoming the tradeoff where existing approaches force you to choose between one or the other.
contributions: Randomized Cholesky factorization algorithm with provable linear-time complexity for efficient preconditioning
Randomized factorization oriented matrix reordering approach to optimize solver performance
Demonstrated superior efficiency achieving 1.51X, 1.93X, and 3.64X speedups over RChol, feGRASS, and AMG based solvers respectively
Practical validation on large-scale power grids with 60 million nodes and 260 million nonzeros

metrics.speedup: 1.51X over RChol, 1.93X over feGRASS, 3.64X over AMG

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
